title: Mi par, che stamattina volentieri
subtitle: Fiordiligi, Dorabella and Don Alfonso: recitative from Così fan tutte, Act 1

licences.source: W. A. Mozart, Così fan tutte, K. 588 (1790), Act 1 scenes 2–3, recitative after No. 4
licences.author: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791)

licences.source: Lorenzo Da Ponte, libretto of Così fan tutte (1790)
licences.author: Lorenzo Da Ponte (1749–1838)
licences.notes: Words as printed in the Peters vocal score (stamattina, Guglielmo, vo, astrologarti, bell' Emme, Pì, Affè, Imenei, perchè). Bars 24–28 follow the print's singer names (Dorabella: Cos' è…, L'amante…; Fiordiligi: L'idol mio…), the other way round from common libretto editions.

licences.source: Edition Peters vocal score (Edition Peters Nr. 4474, plate 11446, edited by Georg Schünemann), pages 31–32, the recitative between No. 4 and No. 5 (29 bars)
licences.author: Kurt Soldan (1891–1946), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: sung lines and piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, then checked bar by bar by a fresh checker (clean). Where the print gives a second rhythm for the German words, the Italian rhythm is kept. The German singing translation is left out. The last bar has two beats and is set as 2/4: it leads attacca subito into No. 5, where Don Alfonso's line ends (fato). Playback tempo ♩ = 110, a nominal speaking pace for secco recitative, from the one separate-track recording found (Böhm, 1:02); Mozart gives no tempo.
